# Issues and Pull Requests

Follow higher-level repository requirements for issue assignment and issue/PR tracking documentation.

## Before any GitHub operation
- Run `gh auth status`. If authenticated, verify the account with `gh api user --jq .login`. If not, ask the user to run `gh auth login`. Git author name or credentials are not a substitute for GitHub CLI authentication.
- If identity or issue information cannot be verified, ask the user. Do not guess.

## Issues
- Before implementation that will become a PR, search for an existing issue: `gh issue list --assignee "@me"` and `gh issue list --state all --search "<keywords>"`. If none exists, ask the user before creating one.
- Keep each issue focused on one independently verifiable outcome.
- Use the template in `skills/git-workflow/templates/issue-template.md` exactly: Title, Type (tick exactly one: Bug, Feature, Enhancement, Task, Documentation), Description, Expected Outcome, Acceptance Criteria (all required), Additional Context (optional, e.g. `ADO: AB#12345`).
- Bug issues also require Environment (Repo, Branch, Environment: Dev / Test / UAT / Prod, plus Browser and OS if applicable), Steps to Reproduce, Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior.
- Replace every line of template guidance text with real content before presenting a draft.

## Pull requests
- Open a PR only after its issue exists. Target `main` unless told otherwise.
- Use `skills/git-workflow/templates/pr-template.md`: Summary, Changes, Related Issue, Testing and Verification, Risks and Performance.
- **Every PR must name its related issue(s)** under `## Related Issue`: `Closes #<n>` when the PR should close the issue, `Refs #<n>` for related issues that stay open, one per line. It must include the issue number from the branch name. A PR without a related issue is not ready.
- Testing and Verification lists real commands and real results. Name anything skipped or failing.
- After opening the PR, update the issue with the PR URL.
- Validate drafts before presenting them: `python skills/git-workflow/scripts/validate_doc.py --kind pr <file> --branch <current-branch>` (issues: `--kind issue <file>`).
- Open the PR with `gh pr create --body-file <validated-file>`. Never use `--fill`, `--web` or an interactive PR: they skip the related-issue check.

## Tracking files
- Keep one tracking file per independent issue in `.thunai/tracking/`: separate, accurate and local-only. Never overwrite unrelated issue files.
- Tracking files are local-only. Never commit or push them (the folder is git-ignored).
